audit_scope.description: Trust model for EIP-158 (empty account clearing), EIP-3041 (eth_getBlockByHash baseFee), EIP-3046 (uncle block baseFee), EIP-3326 (wallet chain switching), and EIP-706 (DEVp2p Snappy compression). Covers state transition rules, RPC response formatting, wallet security, and P2P networking compression.

out_of_scope: Wallet chain switching UI (EIP-3326 - wallet-layer concern)

misclassified_entities.reason: Threat actor (Attacker) from EIP-158 security boundary subgraph is not an external entity - it is a threat model construct representing malicious behavior, not a system boundary entity.

Transaction Sender from EIP-158 is internal to the EL transaction lifecycle - transactions are already validated and included in blocks by the time state clearing occurs. The sender is part of the EVM execution context.
Subprotocol (eth/les) from EIP-706 is internal to the EL networking stack. These are higher-level protocols within the same node, not external entities crossing a trust boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client (EIP-3041)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application or user querying block data via unauthenticated JSON-RPC interface. Can send arbitrary requests including malformed block hashes.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client (EIP-3046)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application querying uncle block information via unauthenticated JSON-RPC interface.

trusted_external_entities.name: Decentralized Application (EIP-3326)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External dapp requesting chain switching. Could be malicious and attempt to trick users into switching to hostile chains or probe wallet capabilities for fingerprinting.

trusted_external_entities.name: Potentially Malicious Dapp (EIP-3326)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Dapp that may attempt to probe wallet capabilities or trick user into switching chains. Privacy fingerprinting risk through chain support enumeration.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node (EIP-706)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote Ethereum node connecting via DEVp2p. Can negotiate protocol version and send compressed messages. Untrusted as any network peer could be malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Interface (EIP-706)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: TCP socket receiving encrypted compressed data
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Raw TCP network interface receiving potentially malicious compressed payloads. Decompression bomb and varint overflow attacks possible.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Peer (EIP-706)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker attempting compression-based DoS attacks via crafted Snappy payloads. Size validation (16MB limit) and varint checks are critical controls.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Client provides block hash and full transaction flag. Node must validate hash format and handle missing blocks gracefully.
Client provides block number and uncle index. Node must validate parameters and return null for non-existent uncles.
Dapp provides target chainId. Wallet must validate format, check registry, and require user confirmation. Privacy leakage via rejection timing must be mitigated.
Peer sends Hello message with version. Version negotiation determines compression. Peer cannot force compression without mutual agreement.
Encrypted bytes received from TCP. Must decrypt, check decompression needed, validate decompressed size <= 16MB before decompressing.
Crafted payloads must be rejected: varint > 2^32-1 causes termination, decompressed_size > 16MB causes rejection. Snappy library assumed free of buffer overflow vulnerabilities.

coverage_gaps: EXT-ATTACKER, EXT-TX-SENDER, EXT-SUBPROTOCOL were misclassified and excluded from boundary analysis
